items.title: Steve Turré interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 29, 2021
items.q: You don’t see Usain Bolt running the 100-meter race anymore, do you? And he’s only 30.

ctx.x: Well I’d like to go back to that for just a second. You’ve already explained it, but it’s so important that you have that focus of why am I doing this and often times I’ve read sociologists and critics who seem to say that musical styles change because of the surroundings that are going on at the time. And I sometimes feel that it doesn’t give enough credit to the musician who is so invested in the music that they are creating these styles because of something that’s inside them.

I think it’s a combination of both things. Because when you look at the world today, totally different than say when Charlie Parker was around or Duke Ellington was around, much less Louis Armstrong. I mean he started out with King Oliver when the world was really a different place. They didn’t even have telephones and you know, not in the households. So they just started to take that stuff on. You know, now we’ve got social media, you know, people when I went to the airport today, checking in you know, and then…

I should ask you about Saturday Night Live a little bit. I’ve wondered, with all that talent that’s been in and out of that band, when a singer, a pop singer comes on and sings along with pre-recorded music and the band is pretending to play — not your band — but the person’s band. I’m wondering what the musicians think about that? © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
